name: Citizenship by Descent

requirements.blocker_text: The 2004 Nationality Code introduced full gender equality: a child born to a Congolese parent (mother or father) acquires Congolese nationality automatically. This replaced an earlier framework that also recognized nationality 'of origin' tied to membership in an ethnic group present in Congolese territory at independence (1960) -- a separate, historically fraught basis distinct from ordinary parent-to-child descent, not modeled as its own route here.

sources.title: Citizenship Rights in Africa Initiative -- report on DRC's 2004 Nationality Code: gender-neutral descent transmission and the separate 'nationality of origin' (ethnic-group-at-independence) basis

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Democratic Republic of the Congo). STATUS: DRAFT -- sourced to an academic citizenship-rights initiative (tier 3) with a Wikipedia cross-reference (tier 4); the 2004 Nationality Code's own government-gazette text was not locatable/fetchable in this build. GENUINE POSITIVE FINDING: descent citizenship is fully gender-neutral since the 2004 reform, consistent with the broader pattern of reformed African nationality laws built elsewhere in this dataset (Kenya, Tanzania). NOT MODELED HERE, DISCLOSED INSTEAD: the separate 'nationality of origin' basis (membership in an ethnic group present in DRC territory at the 1960 independence date) is a historically and politically fraught category tied to DRC's Banyamulenge/Kinyarwanda-speaking-population citizenship disputes -- far more complex than a simple ancestry route and not modeled here given the thin sourcing available in this build; a dedicated follow-up with deeper research would be needed before attempting it. dual_citizenship_allowed left null -- DRC's constitution bans dual nationality but multiple sources describe it as tolerated in practice since 2002 (see cd_citizenship_naturalisation.json's notes for the fuller picture); that law-versus-practice tension is not resolved here, so it is not asserted for a child born with a foreign parent's nationality specifically.
